Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Renewal: capacity bump and term alignment for Aurora Health

Hi David / Jordan,

Quick note — our Q3 forecast just moved up and we need to cover an unexpected lift in inference volume for our patient triage pipelines. We're mid-contract (expires Jan 2028) and want to explore options to add a mid-contract committed uplift and align the renewal date to calendar-year. High-level asks:
- One-page pricing options for an incremental committed uplift of ~35% for the next 6 months (numbers we can present to finance this week).
- Any options to lock a discount if we annualize now and co-term to Jan 2028.
- Confirmation on SLA implications if we add reserved capacity mid-term.

I've attached a brief usage snapshot and our Q3 projection. Can you send an options matrix by end of day Monday? We have a procurement window the week after.

Thanks,
Eleanor Bates
Director of AI Platform
Aurora Health AI

Attachments: Aurora_usage_Q3_v2.csv (summary), Aurora_request_form.pdf
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Bates <eleanor@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:08:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity bump and term alignment for Aurora Health

Eleanor — thanks for the heads up and the data. We can absolutely put together a clean set of options for procurement. High-level we see three viable paths (numbers are illustrative; will confirm after we sync with infra):

Option A — Short-term burst credits
- 35% uplift covered by burst credits invoiced monthly
- No long-term price lock; billed at standard burst rate (no discount)
- Fastest to enable (~48 hours)

Option B — Reserved uplift (recommended for cost predictability)
- Add a 6-month reserved capacity tranche representing ~35% uplift
- 15% discount on token/throughput unit compared to on-demand; credit applied against committed tranche
- SLA remains intact; small provisioning window (2–5 business days) to allocate GPUs

Option C — Annualize and co-term (locks pricing, best unit economics)
- Convert uplift to an annualized add-on and move contract to calendar-year renewal (co-term to Jan 31 2028)
- Deeper discount (we can propose 20%) in exchange for 12-month commit and early PO
- Legal will need to coordinate on amendment and invoicing schedule

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal alignment on which option we want to present (Jordan/Jordan+Grace)
2) I will prepare a one-page options matrix and a draft SOW for Option B and C by EOD tomorrow
3) If Aurora prefers Option C, we will route to Legal for a pricing lock addendum and provide a DocuSign link for PO + amendment

Looping in Grace for pricing verification and Olga for SRE/infra provisioning notes. Jordan — if you prefer a slightly higher discount threshold to push the deal through, flag it and we'll present a playbook with sticker vs. approved pricing.

Thanks — I'll attach the initial workbook and SOW in the next email.

—David
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

David — solid framing. Lean toward Option B as the default (reserved uplift) unless Aurora pushes for annualization. We can sweeten Option B by offering a one-time activation credit equivalent to 5% of the uplift value to accelerate sign-off.

Olga — can you confirm provisioning lead time and any SLA carveouts we should call out? Grace — please validate the 15% discount corridor; escalate to me if we need to widen it to 18% for exec approval.

I'll stand by for the workbook. If Aurora signals urgency, I'm available for a 30-min call Tuesday 13:00–15:00 PT.

—Jordan
